problems.title: Order trigonometric values in mixed angle units
problems.question: Order a=sin7,b=cos280°,c=sin8, with unmarked angles in radians.
problems.idea: Use identities or orthogonal projections, keeping units and domain restrictions explicit.
formulas: Reduce radian angles by 2π; use the degree mark only for 280°.
steps: a≈0.657,b≈0.174,c≈0.989. Therefore b<a<c. The radian remainders are about 41.1° and 98.4°, respectively.

problems.title: Maximum of a squared trigonometric difference
problems.question: Find the maximum of (2sin²3x−2cos²3x)².
problems.idea: Use identities or orthogonal projections, keeping units and domain restrictions explicit.
formulas: $\sin^2t-\cos^2t=-\cos2t$.
steps: The expression is 4cos²6x, bounded above by 4 and attaining 4 when x=0, for example.

problems.title: Order tangent and cotangent values
problems.question: Order a=tan2,b=cot3,c=tan4, with angles in radians.
problems.idea: Use identities or orthogonal projections, keeping units and domain restrictions explicit.
formulas: Tangent is increasing between its poles; cotangent is reciprocal tangent.
steps: a≈−2.185,b≈−7.015,c≈1.158. Thus b<a<c. Both 2 and 3 are in quadrant II, while 4 is in quadrant III.

problems.title: Evenness on symmetric restricted domains
problems.question: Which of f=sinx cosx x³,g=√(cosx),h=tanx cotx are even?
problems.idea: Use identities or orthogonal projections, keeping units and domain restrictions explicit.
formulas: Evenness requires a symmetric domain and $F(-x)=F(x)$.
steps: In f, sinx and x³ are odd and cosx is even, making their product even. g has symmetric domain cosx≥0 and is even.
h equals 1 on its original symmetric domain sinx cosx≠0, so h is also even. Its excluded points do not destroy evenness.
problems.note: No printed choice includes all three. Choices naming only two or one omit another valid even function.

problems.title: A plane normal versus an inclined line
problems.question: One of two skew lines is perpendicular to a plane; the other makes 30° with the plane. Find their angle.
problems.idea: Use identities or orthogonal projections, keeping units and domain restrictions explicit.
formulas: The angle with the plane normal complements the angle with the plane.
steps: The direction angle is 90°−30°=60°. Skew location does not change the angle between line directions.

problems.title: Two perpendicular projections
problems.question: M is 1 from a plane. MA,MB make 45°,60° with the perpendicular MK, and KA⊥KB. Find AB.
problems.idea: Use identities or orthogonal projections, keeping units and domain restrictions explicit.
formulas: $KA=MK\tan45°$, $KB=MK\tan60°$.
steps: KA=1,KB=√3. Their perpendicularity gives AB=√(1+3)=2.

problems.title: A double-angle sine from a ratio
problems.question: sinα is half cosα, with α∈[0°,90°]. Find sin2α.
problems.idea: Use identities or orthogonal projections, keeping units and domain restrictions explicit.
formulas: $\tan\alpha=1/2$ and $\sin2\alpha=2\tan\alpha/(1+\tan^2\alpha)$.
steps: The value is 1/(1+1/4)=4/5=0.8. Neither endpoint fits the original ratio.

problems.title: A line in one face of a dihedral angle
problems.question: A dihedral angle is 45°. A line in one face crosses its edge at 45°. Find its inclination to the other face.
problems.idea: Use identities or orthogonal projections, keeping units and domain restrictions explicit.
formulas: $\sin\theta=\sin(\text{face angle})\sin(\text{line-edge angle})$.
steps: Take the common edge as an axis. The line’s transverse component has magnitude sin45°, and its component normal to the other face is sin45° times that.
Thus sinθ=1/2 and θ=30°, using the line-plane angle range [0°,90°].

problems.title: Two lines perpendicular to a third in space
problems.question: ABC=BCD=90°. What can be said about the angle between AB and CD?
problems.idea: Use identities or orthogonal projections, keeping units and domain restrictions explicit.
formulas: Both direction vectors lie in the plane perpendicular to BC; their relative direction remains free.
steps: Within that perpendicular direction plane they can be parallel, perpendicular, or form any acute line angle. The two given right angles do not determine their mutual angle.
problems.answer: Any line angle from 0° to 90° is possible.

problems.title: Inclination and projected angle
problems.question: An inclined line has plane-angle tangent √5/2. Its projection makes angle φ with an in-plane line, with sinφ=√7/4. Find their line angle.
problems.idea: Use identities or orthogonal projections, keeping units and domain restrictions explicit.
formulas: $\cos\gamma=\cos\theta\,|\cos\varphi|$; $\cos\theta=1/\sqrt{1+\tan^2\theta}$.
steps: cosθ=2/3 and |cosφ|=√(1−7/16)=3/4. Therefore cosγ=1/2, giving γ=60°.

problems.title: Period after two argument changes
problems.question: f(x)=g(0.5x)+h(2x),g(x)=sin4x,h(x)=cosx. Find its least positive period.
problems.idea: Use identities or orthogonal projections, keeping units and domain restrictions explicit.
formulas: $f(x)=\sin2x+\cos2x=\sqrt2\sin(2x+\pi/4)$.
steps: Its angular frequency is 2, so least positive period=2π/2=π.

problems.title: Mixed radian and degree reductions
problems.question: Evaluate tan(−π+1)sin900°+cot(−675°)−sin²(20π/7)−cos²(6π/7).
problems.idea: Use identities or orthogonal projections, keeping units and domain restrictions explicit.
formulas: Use periodicity and $\sin^2t+\cos^2t=1$.
steps: sin900°=0 and cot(−675°)=cot45°=1. Reducing 20π/7 by 2π gives 6π/7.
The final two terms sum to −1, so the total is 0+1−1=0.

problems.title: A shifted sine identity
problems.question: Express sin(3π/2+α) in one of the listed equivalent forms.
problems.idea: Use identities or orthogonal projections, keeping units and domain restrictions explicit.
formulas: $\sin(3\pi/2+\alpha)=-\cos\alpha$.
steps: Also sin(α−π/2)=−cosα. Therefore this is the matching listed expression for every real α.

problems.title: A projected isosceles triangle
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has sides 6,6,3√2; equal side BC lies in a plane, AB makes 30° with it, and AK is perpendicular to the plane. Find BKC.
problems.idea: Use identities or orthogonal projections, keeping units and domain restrictions explicit.
formulas: AB=BC=6,AC=3√2; projection lengths follow Pythagoras.
steps: Under the intended labelling AB=BC=6,AC=3√2, AK=AB sin30°=3. Hence BK²=27 and CK²=9. Their sum is BC²=36, giving BKC=90°.
The wording only identifies BC as an equal side. If instead AC=BC=6 and AB=3√2, then AK²=9/2, BK²=27/2, CK²=63/2. The cosine rule gives cos BKC=1/√21, a different feasible angle.
problems.note: A unique 90° answer requires AB=BC, or an equivalent apex/base label. Stating only that BC is an equal side leaves another labelling possible.

problems.title: Two sum-to-product simplifications
problems.question: Simplify [cos(π/4+α)+cos(π/4−α)]/(√2cosα)+√2[sin(π/6−α)+sin(π/6+α)]/[sin(π/4−α)+sin(π/4+α)].
problems.idea: Use identities or orthogonal projections, keeping units and domain restrictions explicit.
formulas: $\cos(u+v)+\cos(u-v)=2\cos u\cos v$; $\sin(u+v)+\sin(u-v)=2\sin u\cos v$.
steps: The first fraction is √2cosα/(√2cosα)=1. The second term is √2·cosα/(√2cosα)=1.
Total=2 on the original domain cosα≠0.

problems.title: Resolve quarter-angles using their intervals
problems.question: cos(α/4)=1/2,cos(β/4)=−√2/2,1080°<α<1440°,720°<β<1080°. Find tan[(360°−α−β)/4].
problems.idea: Use identities or orthogonal projections, keeping units and domain restrictions explicit.
formulas: Use the specified quadrants before substituting the exact angles.
steps: The requested angle is −435°, equivalent to −75° for tangent. tan75°=2+√3, so the answer is −2−√3.

problems.title: Area between two projection segments
problems.question: AB=3 is parallel to a plane at distance √3. Inclined AC,BD are perpendicular in direction to AB and meet the plane at angles 60°,30°. Find area of quadrilateral A₁B₁DC, with A₁,B₁ the perpendicular feet.
problems.idea: Use identities or orthogonal projections, keeping units and domain restrictions explicit.
formulas: Projection length $=h/\tan\theta$; trapezoid area = half the base sum times separation.
steps: A₁C=√3/tan60°=1 and B₁D=√3/tan30°=3. These projection segments are parallel and perpendicular to A₁B₁, whose length is AB=3.
For the stated ordinary, non-self-crossing quadrilateral, they are its two bases. Area=(1+3)×3/2=6.

problems.title: Range of a quotient of square roots
problems.question: Find the range of √(0.5−x³)/√(0.5+x³).
problems.idea: Use identities or orthogonal projections, keeping units and domain restrictions explicit.
formulas: Domain $-0.5<x^3\le0.5$. Square the nonnegative quotient to get $(0.5-t)/(0.5+t)$, t=x³.
steps: The squared value decreases continuously from arbitrarily large positive values to 0 as t goes from just above −0.5 to 0.5.
Taking nonnegative square roots gives the full range [0,∞).

problems.title: Two forty-five-degree lines in perpendicular planes
problems.question: Two planes meet at 90°. Each contains a line meeting their common edge at 45°. Find the smaller angle between the lines.
problems.idea: Use identities or orthogonal projections, keeping units and domain restrictions explicit.
formulas: Use the edge as z-axis; unit directions have components $(\pm1/\sqrt2,0,\pm1/\sqrt2)$ and $(0,\pm1/\sqrt2,\pm1/\sqrt2)$.
steps: Their dot product has absolute value 1/2. Thus the smaller line angle is arccos(1/2)=60°, independently of the signs.

problems.title: Tangent addition cancels a product
problems.question: Simplify [tanα+tan(45°−α)]/[1−tanαtan(45°−α)]−tanαtanβ−(tanα+tanβ)cot(α+β).
problems.idea: Use identities or orthogonal projections, keeping units and domain restrictions explicit.
formulas: The first fraction is tan45°=1; addition gives $(\tan\alpha+\tan\beta)\cot(\alpha+\beta)=1-\tan\alpha\tan\beta$.
steps: The expression is 1−tanαtanβ−[1−tanαtanβ]=0 wherever all original terms and denominators are defined.

problems.title: A reciprocal pair of squared tangents
problems.question: Find the minimum of 8tan²x+18cot²(−x).
problems.idea: Use identities or orthogonal projections, keeping units and domain restrictions explicit.
formulas: Put t=tan²x>0; cot²(−x)=1/t and AM–GM applies.
steps: 8t+18/t≥2√144=24. Equality requires 8t=18/t, so t=3/2, achievable for real x in the original domain.

problems.title: A fourth-angle sine from cotangent
problems.question: cot(π/2+α)=2. Find sin4α.
problems.idea: Use identities or orthogonal projections, keeping units and domain restrictions explicit.
formulas: $\cot(\pi/2+\alpha)=-\tan\alpha$; $\sin2\alpha=2t/(1+t^2)$, $\cos2\alpha=(1-t^2)/(1+t^2)$.
steps: t=tanα=−2, so sin2α=−4/5 and cos2α=−3/5.
sin4α=2sin2αcos2α=24/25.

problems.title: A bisector condition forces perpendicular projections
problems.question: M is distance h from a plane with perpendicular foot K. MA=a,MB=b are inclined segments. The bisector of MAK is perpendicular in direction to KB. Find AB.
problems.idea: Use identities or orthogonal projections, keeping units and domain restrictions explicit.
formulas: The bisector direction from A is the sum of unit vectors along AM and AK.
steps: Take the plane as z=0,K=0. If A’s planar vector is u and |u|=p=√(a²−h²), the planar component of that bisector is −u(1/a+1/p).
Its perpendicularity to KB therefore forces u·KB=0: projections KA and KB are perpendicular.
Hence AB²=KA²+KB²=(a²−h²)+(b²−h²), giving AB=√(a²+b²−2h²).

problems.title: Choose signs in two half-angle formulas
problems.question: If cos2020°=a, express cos505°.
problems.idea: Use identities or orthogonal projections, keeping units and domain restrictions explicit.
formulas: $\cos(\theta/2)=\pm\sqrt{(1+\cos\theta)/2}$, with sign chosen from the quadrant.
steps: 1010° is equivalent to 290°, so cos1010°>0 and equals √[(1+a)/2].

problems.title: Centroid distances using signed heights
problems.question: A,B,C are distances 1,2,3 from a plane, possibly on different sides. Which listed distance 2,4/3,2/3,0,1 cannot occur for their centroid?
problems.idea: Use identities or orthogonal projections, keeping units and domain restrictions explicit.
formulas: Signed centroid height $=(\pm1\pm2\pm3)/3$; distance is its absolute value.
steps: The possible absolute sums are 0,2,4,6, giving distances 0,2/3,4/3,2.
Distance 1 is absent. Each sign pattern can be realized by choosing noncollinear horizontal positions.
